customer.business: Always Broke Ltd: a permanent holding company that buys owner-managed small and micro businesses and keeps their management and culture
customer.target: Owner-managers of profitable small German businesses (roughly EUR 100k to 400k EBITDA) who want to hand over within about five years and have no successor

market_context.text: 57% of German SME owners are 55 or older and 545,000 SMEs want a successor by the end of 2029; one in four SMEs is considering closure
Sellers' average asking price is about EUR 499,000, median EUR 375,000; price agreement is a hurdle in about a third of cases, and many owners start with inflated expectations
A sale's sales phase takes roughly 6 to 18 months and the buyer's house bank decides financing separately
Many owners distrust financial investors, mainly for their reputation, and worry about staff
The state-backed nexxt-change exchange lists businesses for free and anonymously, so sellers have a free way to look for buyers

segments.name: Craft and trade business
segments.sector: Skilled trade or service business with 5 to 25 staff

segments.name: Niche B2B product or service firm
segments.sector: Specialist supplier, distributor or service firm

segments.name: Local retail, hospitality or consumer service
segments.sector: One or a few sites serving local customers

segments.name: Owner-dependent micro firm
segments.sector: Under 5 staff, value tied to the owner's personal relationships

roles.name: Owner-manager
roles.how: Decides personally and emotionally; the business is their life's work.

roles.name: Owner with spouse or co-owner
roles.how: Both must agree; the spouse often worries about retirement income.

roles.name: Owner guided by tax adviser or lawyer
roles.how: Asks the adviser to test any buyer's credibility and structure.

buying_process.name: Owner decides after meeting the buyer
buying_process.how: Wants to meet the person, visit the site and hear what happens to the staff.

buying_process.name: Adviser or broker runs a process
buying_process.how: Collects offers, asks for proof of funds and for references.

buying_process.name: Bank and adviser vet the buyer first
buying_process.how: Checks buyer identity, funding and structure before sharing any numbers.

buying_process.name: Family or management buyout preferred
buying_process.how: Only talks to an outside buyer if the internal route fails.

current_options.name: Hand over to family or an internal successor
current_options.how: Often at a low or gifted price, if a successor exists.

current_options.name: Sell to a trade buyer, a management buyer or via a broker or nexxt-change
current_options.how: At about the median asking price; price talks and financing are the usual hurdle.

current_options.name: Close the business or keep running without a plan
current_options.how: Wind down, sell the equipment, or keep working past retirement age.

behaviours.name: Price-led seller
behaviours.how: Takes the highest cash offer, whatever the buyer's plans.

behaviours.name: Continuity-led seller
behaviours.how: Cares most that staff, name and location stay.

behaviours.name: Cautious seller
behaviours.how: Distrusts new or unusual buyers and wants proof, references and a bank letter.

objections.text: I do not know a Belize holding company; who stands behind it and where do I take a claim if it goes wrong?

objections: You have no track record, no named funders and no proof of funds

objections.text: I expect a higher price; others will pay more in cash at closing
What happens to my staff and my customers after I go?
Why would my bank, tax adviser and notary accept a buyer like this?

objections: Part of the price deferred or in a seller note puts my retirement money at risk

benchmark_rate.what: assumed share of approached owners who sign a deal within a year (no sourced benchmark found; this is a placeholder)

pitch:
Always Broke Ltd, a newly formed Belize-incorporated holding company, buys profitable owner-managed small businesses in the EU and keeps them for the long term. There is no planned resale.
We buy 100% of the business, keep your management team, staff, name and location, and do not impose a restructuring.
Indicative price: about 3.5x to 4.5x yearly EBITDA after due diligence (for example, about EUR 700,000 to 900,000 for EUR 200,000 EBITDA). Terms are open to discussion.
Payment: about 70% in cash at closing, 30% over three years. You stay for a handover of up to 12 months, paid.
Honest status: we have no track record yet and funding for the first deal is not yet committed. We will share proof of funds and the structure with your adviser before you sign anything. A confidential first meeting costs nothing.
